long_description.before:
MindFort is building fully autonomous AI agents powered by their in-house models that can find, exploit, and patch complex vulnerabilities in web applications at massive scale. MindFort agents use the same principles as human penetration testers to understand their target and figure out the best ways to work together to exploit it. We can do fully autonomous AI web pentesting and bring offensive security to teams out numbered. 

While security teams were already behind with legacy tools and processes, AI coding is make the problem worse. AI generates code far faster than human teams can secure it; MindFort can match that speed and scale. Our agents will become critical as organizations scale up development with AI.

long_description.before:
Cardboard is an agentic video editor for growth/marketing teams and serious creators who need to ship videos consistently. Instead of agencies, long timelines, and infinite review cycles, teams give cardboard a footage + a goal (“3 variants”, “30s hook”, “testimonials”) to get a strong first cut in minutes on which they can iterate quickly.

Multimodal LLMs can finally reason over footage, and WebGPU/WebCodecs make a real NLE possible in the browser. For the first time, an “AI director” inside a professional editor can be a reality.

We have to build two hard things at once: a high-performance editor in the browser and an agentic editor that is reliable for production use cases. Most startups do one; incumbents can’t rebuild their stack without breaking everything.

Saksham and Ishan met in school and have known each other since 15 years. Saksham was Co-founder/CTO of Iterate AI (backed by EF) and posts content on social media; Ishan has spent ~5yr building memory-heavy, performance-critical browser apps at HackerRank (S11) and deeply understands browsers. He has built Hotspoter (5M+ downloads) when he was 14.

Together, we’re unusually suited to build the editor core others avoid.

Video is becoming the default distribution channel, and the team that iterates fastest compounds attention. Cardboard becomes the default workspace for video production, the way Canva/Figma became the workspace for design - because it’s collaborative, fast, and does the tedious parts for you.
long_description.after:
Cardboard (cardboard.ai) is an AI video editor that turns raw footage into finished videos, from social clips and highlight reels to product demos, launch videos and event recaps. Describe the video you want, and Cardboard turns your clips, photos, recordings or a link into an edit you can watch, change and export, in the browser, in the Mac app, or right inside ChatGPT and Claude. It pulls out the best moments, removes pauses and filler words, adds captions, titles, music and B-roll, and reframes for Reels, Shorts and TikTok. It’s built for marketing teams, founders and creators who need video every week without learning a timeline.

Say what you need, like “three 30-second ad variants” or “a customer testimonial from these interviews”, and Cardboard’s AI agent, Director, builds a first cut in minutes. You refine it by chatting or on a full timeline, with your team. Cardboard edits the footage you already have. Unlike AI video generators such as Runway or Sora, it doesn’t create new video from a text prompt.

- Recreate the style of a reference video with your own footage.
- Make motion graphics from a prompt, from animated titles to 3D scenes like a spinning product shot.
- Cut to the beat, with match cuts, transitions and effects synced to the music.
- 80+ ready-made recipes (templates) for videos like launch videos, product showcases, podcast clips, webinar highlights, and testimonials.
- Export the finished video, or hand the timeline off to Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Why now: AI models can finally understand video, and WebGPU makes a professional editor possible in a browser tab. Most AI video tools are either an old editor with AI bolted on, or an agent with no real editor behind it. Cardboard is built to be both.

Team: Saksham Aggarwal (CEO) and Ishan Sharma (CTO) have been friends for 15 years, since school. Saksham studied computer science at BITS Pilani, was co-founder and CTO of Iterate AI (backed by Entrepreneur First), and worked in growth at Sequoia-backed Flint. Ishan spent nearly five years building performance-critical browser apps at HackerRank (YC S11), and at 14 built Hotspoter, a Windows app with over 5 million downloads.

Together, they are unusually suited to build the editor core others avoid.

Video is becoming the default distribution channel, and the team that iterates fastest compounds attention. Cardboard becomes the default workspace for video production, the way Canva/Figma became the workspace for design - because it’s collaborative, fast, and does the tedious parts for you.

(formerly usecardboard.com or cardboard.sh)

one_liner.after: AI video editor (raw footage into finished videos)

long_description.before:
Memoir is a video call with a proactive AI teammate built in. While people talk, it picks up the work hiding in the conversation and starts on it, in real time. Say "let me pull up the pricing deck" and it appears on your screen. Say "let's sketch the architecture" and a diagram draws itself for everyone. Ask "Memoir, what did we decide on pricing?" and it answers out loud from the call itself, with context gathered beforehand.

When the call ends, the follow-ups are already written: the email to the customer, the calendar hold, the reminder, each one click to send. The work that usually waits hours after a meeting, or never happens, is ready before you hang up.

Agents already work in our inboxes, browsers and code editors. Calls are where teams make decisions, and agents still aren't in the room. We're starting with technical founders on the sales and design calls they host, where a slow follow-up costs a deal, and building toward calls where people and agents work side by side.
long_description.after:
Memoir is an AI teammate that joins your video calls, listens like everyone else, and only talks when you talk to it.

A founder is on a sales call. The customer asks what a pilot would look like. Instead of promising to send something over, the founder says, "Memoir, draft this up." A few seconds later there's a page in the chat with the plan they just talked through. Everyone opens it, and they go through it together before anyone hangs up. Afterward, Memoir can help the founder follow up on what they promised, with one click.

Most calls end with a list of things people said they'd do, and it takes days to do them. Agents already do real work in our email, our browsers and our code. They've become extensions of us. But on calls, most of them still just take notes.

We're starting with technical founders on the sales and design calls they run in Google Meet. But we want every call to work like that one. Eventually everyone will bring their own agents to a call, and those agents will work together the way the people do.

one_liner.before: The Zoom alternative where agents build what you discuss in real time
one_liner.after: An AI teammate that answers and builds live on your calls

We are a team of ex-intelligence, ex-finance, and most importantly, ex-founders who have known each other for over 5 years.

Collar is redefining investor relations.

They have a bird’s eye view of what external stakeholders want, and also work with internal business units to create a grand vision of a company’s future.

But they’re doing it with their hands tied behind their back.

Finance AI tools today are built for investors not investor relations, leaving teams using ad-hoc unreliable workarounds, and CFOs are stuck always reporting rather than acting on insights to optimize operational workstreams.

After earning calls, CFOs use Collar’s trusted agentic AI systems to optimize identified underperforming workstreams with little manual modification needed. 

Redefining investor relations from a tedious cost centre headache, into a whole-of-company profit maximising function.

long_description.before:
Ascenix is the all-in-one incident platform that turns unstructured EHR data into automated reporting, reimbursement recovery, compliance flagging, and clinical insight. We’re already live in 50 homes and scaling across North America. We connect to systems like PointClickCare and analyze the notes nurses already write, adapting to any note structure and any compliance or reporting requirement.

We help teams identify documentation gaps, uncover missed revenue opportunities and spot emerging resident risks, while reducing time spent reviewing charts and building spreadsheets. Our goal is to improve residents’ quality of life by helping care homes reach their full clinical, financial and operational potential.
long_description.after:
Ascenix is building custom software for running senior homes. We combine reusable building blocks into workflows tailored to each home's existing processes, from incident reporting to reimbursement. Homes get custom software without hiring an engineering team.

Living in a retirement home convinced us that the best way to improve residents' lives is to improve the systems staff rely on. As the older population grows, care teams need more time and resources. Repetitive reporting, missed reimbursement, and compliance problems take those away, while disconnected tools add costs and leave staff moving information between systems.

Our building blocks gather information from EHRs like PointClickCare and other sources, process it, apply rules, and produce reports, tasks, or emails. Incident reporting and reimbursement reviews usually come from two separate vendors. Ascenix builds both from the same blocks, in one interface, so data isn't stuck in silos. Homes start with their biggest bottleneck and add workflows as priorities change.

one_liner.before: Clinical intelligence layer for skilled nursing facilities.
one_liner.after: One interface for senior care facilities.
